title: Succession certificate vs legal heir certificate - the difference clients confuse
p1:
Many people think a legal heir certificate and a succession certificate are the same thing.

They are not. And choosing the wrong one can delay the process when dealing with a deceased person's assets.
p2:
A legal heir certificate mainly identifies who the legal heirs of a person are. It is often used for purposes like transferring certain records, pensions, or family-related claims.

A succession certificate goes a step further. It is generally used to establish the right to collect debts and securities, such as bank deposits, shares, or other financial assets, especially when there is no separate nomination or transfer process available.
p3:
The surprising part? Having your name listed as a legal heir does not automatically give you the authority to collect every financial asset left behind.

The right certificate depends on what needs to be transferred and what legal proof is required. A small mistake at this stage can create unnecessary court visits and delays.
